title: Apply Two-Variable Relationships to Solve Problems
objective: I can write an equation to represent the relationship between two variable quantities and use it to solve a real problem.
model: four linked representations of one relationship (scenario, table, graph, equation); substitute to predict, work backward to solve, interpret in context

widgets.component: table to equation, d = 12h, y = 5x at x = 6, which variable is alone
widgets.root: Identical to the config warm-up; keys verified (y = 4x, d = 12h, 30, dependent).

widgets.component: assembly line c = 2.5h, car wash $12 a car, bakery c = 2n + 10 versus c = 2.5n, 'at least' goals, rounding in context, compare two plans
widgets.root: Keys recomputed (20 cars, 400 hours, about 17 days, 42 cars, $14.29, 50 cupcakes against 44, 13 hours, 19 hours, Robot Y costs $40 against $44). The two-step bakery equation c = 2n + 10 is the lesson's own Connect scenario and 'Work backward' is in its vocabulary, so solving it is in scope.

widgets.where: Practice 2.7 (sort true or false) and Challenge 3.3 (sort stages of solving)
widgets.component: true or false statements about c = 2.5h; substitute, solve, check and interpret for c = 6h + 14
widgets.root: Bins verified (4 hours gives 10 cars true, 2 hours gives 4 false, c is the input false). Stage sort matches the lesson's key idea: substitute, solve, interpret.

widgets.component: equation given, solve for the input; read the input off a graph or table; least whole value that reaches a goal; compare two plans at one input
widgets.root: 7 seeds at each level: answers right (e = 8h gives 13 at 104, 3p ≥ 35 gives 12, Plan B 7 per mile gives $70 against $90). Tables and coordinate graphs render correctly.

widgets.component: plot the pairs from a rule; at L4 the y-values are given and the student works backward to x
widgets.root: Table and graph are two of the four representations the lesson links; the reversed L4 form is the lesson's 'work backward'. It does not itself ask for a predicted value.

widgets.component: round down for 'at least', subtract before dividing, substitute into the wrong variable
widgets.root: Error steps right (index 2, 1, 1). Values recomputed (15, 20/12/36/36/52/60, 7, 15.39, 13 hours). Wording in 5.4 ('the least price in whole cents, in dollars') is muddled but the key is right.

widgets.component: 'The solution to one problem was 41.7 cars. Would producing or washing a PARTIAL car make sense?'
widgets.root: The unseen problem decides the answer: if the council NEEDS at least 41.7 cars' worth, round up (the keyed answer), but if it can only AFFORD 41.7 cars, round down, which is distractor 3. With no problem on screen, two choices are defensible.
widgets.replacement: Give the problem: 'The council needs at least $500 at $12 a car, so 12n ≥ 500 and n ≈ 41.7 cars. What should it do about the 0.7 of a car?' with choices 'Round up to 42, because 41 cars raise only $492', 'Round down to 41, because 0.7 of a car cannot be washed', 'Wash 41.7 cars', 'The equation is wrong'.

formulaOrder.formula: c = 2n + 10 (rate times input plus a fixed fee), solved by working backward

typography: twoVarProblem stems print 'the Ana\'s age', 'the today\'s temperature', 'the yesterday\'s temperature', 'The Leo\'s score', 'the Mia\'s score' (a possessive after 'the'), which reads as broken English to a student (Practice 4.1-4.6, Challenge 1.1-1.6)
Challenge 5.4 asks for 'the least price in whole cents, in dollars', an awkward phrase for the answer 15.39
